name: Hartwick College
overview:
Hartwick College is a private liberal arts college in Oneonta, New York. The institution's origin is rooted in the founding of Hartwick Seminary in 1797 through the will of John Christopher Hartwick.

In 1927, the Seminary moved to expand into a four-year college and was offered land by the city of Oneonta to move to its current location. The college has 1,103 undergraduate students from 30 states and 22 countries, 187 faculty members, and a student-faculty ratio of 11:1.
administrative:
1. Application (work directly with Hartwick)

  • Official Transcripts in English (stamped & signed by home institution)
  • Passport copy (valid 6 months after the program end date)
  • Proof of Financial Support in English
  • Health Insurance is mandatory


2. Reception of the letter of acceptance from the partner university

Once you are admitted by the host university, Hartwick will send us your admission package with your acceptance letter & original documents for your visa. You can request a visa only after your application has been approved.


3. Visa

You can find all the detailed information on the US government website or the Embassy of the US in Paris website. You can check the deadlines for obtaining an appointment here.


1/Admission letter and I-20 form

When you have been admitted to CSU LB, you will receive an acceptance letter and an I-20 form, allowing you to apply for the F-1 student visa at the embassy. Please check the information on I-20 carefully and sign the document.


2/Pay the SEVIS fees

 You must then pay the SEVIS I-901 fees online (here). Make sure you print the receipts. The fees for students are $350.


3/Complete the DS-160 form

Complete DS-160 form and upload an ID photo meeting the following requirements. Print the application form confirmation page to bring to your interview.

You will have to pay a visa application fee (non refundable) before your interview of $185 (more information here).


4/Schedule an appointment at the consulate

For people in France, you need to make an appointment for your interview at the US Consulate. Plan to travel to Paris for it.

If you live in another country, check the different consulate/embassy.


During your interview at the consulate, you must:

  • have the necessary supporting documents to prove that you qualify for the category of visa that you request--document relating to your current studies and its relationship to the studies you wish to pursue in the United States: academic transcript, various certificates, SAT or TOEFL test scores, diplomas, etc.
  • demonstrate, with supporting evidence, to the consular officer that you have solid family, social and financial ties to France and that you intend to return there once your residence permit has expired.
  • prove that you have the financial means necessary to finance your studies and live in good conditions in the United States for the first 12 months. Any document proving your family or relational ties with any person funding your studies, as well as bank statements, tax notices thereof.

Please note that the visa gives you the right to work 20 hours on campus.


4. Insurance and health

Option 1: insurance recommended by Hartwick

International students have the option of choosing health insurance plans that are recommended by Hartwick, or they can choose a health insurance provider from their home country. The International Student Office at Hartwick is happy to assist you in finding the perfect fit for your health insurance provider.


Option 2: private international insurance

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country’s health file at: https://www.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fr/conseils-aux-voyageurs/conseils-par-pays-destination/etats-unis/


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

Students will be in on-campus housing and must sign up for the meal plan (on-campus dining hall). There is a fee of 17,000 USD that covers housing and the meal plan for the entire year.


The residences with double occupancy that students are likely to be placed in are Saxton Hall, Wilder Hall, Holmes Hall, Smith Hall, Van Ess Hall, Oyaron House and Hilltop House. (As Leitzell Hall, The Townhouses and the Day Apartments are offered to full time Juniors and Seniors on priority). Students can certainly indicate their preference for which hall they would like to be in, and we can work with our Res Life to help process that request, though it may not always be guaranteed.


Each double occupancy dorm room includes 2 of the following: Bed, nightstand, desk, chair and dresse. Typically for bed sheets (and bed-in-a-bag), students can order these ahead of time through Dormify, or if they arrive on campus in time, we usually are able to go to Walmart to purchase these. However, we are starting to collaborate with our event coordinator to access rental sheets, and we can request that graduating or leaving students donate furniture such as desk lamps for Northeast Experience students to use moving forward.


All Northeast students get the All-Access plan which includes 3 meals per weekday and 2 meals per day (brunch and dinner) on Saturdays and Sundays.

Financial Overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).
